mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 3% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals labor market distress, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month periods of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single meeting, followed by a pause, signals a policy shift toward easing, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS cut > 0.50% in one meeting, then no change next meeting
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive after a >0.50% FEDFUNDS cut followed by a pause.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months—where PAYEMS rises while UNRATE falls—signals labor market normalization, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls concurrently for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the real savings rate (RSAFS) above its long-run average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces household consumption and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > long-run average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its long-run average for six consecutive months.
